notes.title: Training mode and Campaign mode in Math Challenge AR
notes.content:
Math Challenge AR has two game modes, which we will see below, and which have some important differences that are worth knowing. Leaving aside the typical tutorial of course, which you can run whenever you want. Let's take a look at it below.

[previewyoutube=AxmZTF8F86g;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Training mode.[/b]

The training mode allows the player to configure the game to his liking, with the exact parameters that he decides at each moment. To do this, just enter the configuration screen, adapt the game elements, and start training. Some of the parameters in the configuration screen are self-explanatory. Others deserve an explanation. All of this can be read in the game manual, where the function of each of these parameters is explained in detail.

Once the player is satisfied with a configuration, at the start of a training session the player will play with those parameters set. In that way, the player can modify the type of mathematical operations, the maximum playing time, whether there will be negatives or decimals in the operations, how many digits each operation will have, or more general things such as the speed of rotation of the static panels, or the speed at which the numbers move. Even if you want some help during the game, something that can come in handy for the little ones in the house.

The training mode stores the results of a game session, and displays them at the end of the training session. You can also view those results at any time from the settings screen.

What training mode does not do is earn achievements. Achievements are reserved for the campaign mode, which we will see below.

[b]Campaign mode in Math Challenge AR.[/b]

The campaign mode in Math Challenge AR works in a different way than the training mode. What it does is to start at level one, and reconfigures the game internally so that the difficulty increases with each new level. It is important to note that it does not touch the settings on the configuration screen. What it does is to ignore those parameters, and thus starts a campaign that, in the first levels, will be very easy, but will become more complex during the development of the campaign.

How many levels are there in the campaign? There is no limit. It is true that after certain levels the game will not be more complex and difficult, but overcoming each level will be a challenge. Of course, the player can continue passing levels as long as he wants, and there will be no limit.

[b]The awards associated with the campaign mode.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/2425fd6cab24cf2ded0a3083faf3301b36266c32.png[/img]

With the development of the campaign the player will go through different ranks, until reaching the maximum. There are sixteen possible ranks.

[b]Patch:[/b] it is obtained by earning points. The campaign bar with the cap symbol will be filled as the player gets closer to the next award. When it arrives, the award will be activated and the bar will start filling up again.

The stars in each patch will only be visible if the point level of the patch has been reached. The colors indicate different awards:

* Blue: activated when a number of solved static panels has been exceeded. Remember that the static panels must be solved to finish the training at the level of the campaign you are playing.
* Green: it is activated when a number of dynamic panels have been passed.
* Yellow: it is activated when you have passed a number of point panels.
* Red: activated when a number of enemy ships have been destroyed. This requires playing with the enemies mode logically activated.

It is important to note that, even if a patch has been activated, the stars will not appear until the number of elements necessary to activate that star has been obtained. But, if you have not obtained the points to activate a patch, the stars, even if they are active, will not appear. You will have to combine points and stars to get all the prizes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45614163/21c9ff4e982160a78ad0c77534be3b18b2302393.png[/img]

The upper bar controls the power you have for your lasers. The middle one your health. And the last one, visible only in Campaign, indicates the points you need to get the next awards.

[b]Ending the game.
[/b]
Oh, and one important thing: if you run out of health in the game during a level, all points earned from that level are lost. Not the previous ones, but the ones earned in that level. So you will have to finish that level to be able to add up the points.

And that's all on the subject of Math Challenge AR's training and campaign modes. Now it's up to you, let math be with you!
